tip: Formal commands put the verb first, then Sie: Entschuldigen Sie means excuse me, addressed politely.
To negate a whole noun, German uses kein instead of nicht: keine Hilfe means no help.
The du command drops the -st ending and the pronoun: du schläfst becomes just schlaf.
A modal like kann pushes the main verb to the very end as an infinitive: kann heute nicht kommen.
For things, not people, German fuses da plus a preposition: darüber means about it, replacing über plus it.
Strong verbs with a in the stem add an umlaut in the er/sie form: graben becomes vergräbt, he or she buries.
Schulden means debts and exists only in the plural; the singular Schuld means guilt or fault instead.
Bescheid bekommen is a set phrase meaning to get word or be informed; Bescheid stays capitalized and unchanged.
Add -d to a verb to build a present participle used like an adjective: schnurren gives schnurrenden, purring.
niemand takes case endings like an article; the dative object here is niemandem, meaning to nobody.
A few countries carry an article: die Schweiz. To say in it, use the dative, in der Schweiz.
sich beschweren is reflexive and means to complain; the sich is required, as in hat sich beschwert.
Add -in to a job noun to make it female: Gärtner becomes Gärtnerin, a female gardener.
heißen means to be called, so Ich heiße Anna is literally I am called Anna, the normal way to give your name.
To say you like doing something, add gern to the verb: trinkt gern means likes to drink.
zufrieden mit means satisfied with, and mit always takes the dative: mit dem Ergebnis.
The diminutive ending -chen always makes a noun neuter: das Glühwürmchen, even though a Wurm is masculine.
weder and noch work as a pair meaning neither and nor: weder Fisch noch Fleisch.
Comparatives add -er and use als for than: schwieriger als erwartet, more difficult than expected.
With seit for ongoing time, German uses the present tense where English uses have been: seit fünfzehn Jahren.
auf takes the dative when it marks location without movement: liegt auf dem Küchentisch.
With a time, erst means not until: öffnet erst Mitte Mai means it opens no sooner than mid-May.
German uses machen, to make, for earning a license: den Führerschein machen means to pass your driving test.
With a clock time, gegen means around, not against: gegen elf Uhr is about eleven o'clock.
erklären gives the person the dative, dem Schüler, while the thing explained stays accusative.
Some masculine nouns add -en in every case except the nominative: der Komet becomes einen Kometen.
German has no -ing form; gerade plus the present shows an action in progress: renovieren gerade, renovating right now.
